subject: Unexpected 429s during customer test window — mitigation and remediation plan
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex@brightlayer.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@brightlayer.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: 429s during our scheduled integration test window

Hi Laura,

We ran the scheduled integration test this afternoon (simulating 5k concurrent users over 30 minutes) and started seeing a sharp rise in 429 responses around 15 minutes in. Error rate went from ~0.5% to ~12% and stayed elevated for about 10 minutes before falling back. We've attached a small curl log and our client-side retry traces (retry-logs-20270903.zip).

This was really disruptive to our validation: many of our worker jobs hit exponential backoff and caused a large ingestion lag. Can your team confirm if this was a config change on your side or a mis-match in our request window sizing? The logs show headers: x-rw-tenant-id: BL-1321 and x-rw-model: redwood-llama-13b-v2.

We need a remediation plan and a timeline for credits/rollback if this is on Redwood's side. happy to jump on a call.

— Alex

From: laura.bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@brightlayer.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: 429s during our scheduled integration test window

Hi Alex — thanks for the details and the logs. I'm escalating to our infra team and looping in Rishi and Ben for immediate investigation.

Quick notes:
- We see the tenant ID in our telemetry and a concurrent burst at 15:12 PDT.
- Can you confirm the exact client retry policy (initial wait, multiplier, max attempts)? That will help us understand amplification.

We will investigate whether a routing change or a temporary quota window misalignment caused the spike. I'll follow up in 90 minutes with an initial read and next steps.

— Laura
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 18:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: 429s during our scheduled integration test window

Team — quick internal findings after an initial sweep:
- Root cause (prelim): a configuration drift in the tenant-rate-window map during a deploy to routing service INF-RTR-3. A new hyphenation rule incorrectly collapsed two adjacent tenant windows which resulted in BL-1321 being counted in the shorter 60s enforcement window instead of the intended 5m window.
- Effect: the shorter enforcement window reduced the effective token allowance during bursty patterns, and with BrightLayer's aggressive client retries we observed transient queue saturation and 429 propagation.
- Impact scope: only tenants routed through INF-RTR-3 between 15:10–15:24 PDT (we have a list of ~18 tenants; BrightLayer is the highest-volume affected).

Immediate remediation steps applied (15:48 PDT):
1) Rolled back the routing rule to prior stable (INF-RTR-3@rev-198).
2) Manually cleared the enforcement counters for BL-1321 and the other affected tenants to let them reaccumulate quota.
3) Placed a temporary higher burst allowance for BL-1321 for the remainder of the test window.

Follow-ups: we'll produce a detailed remediation playbook and a postmortem doc. Attaching initial playbook: remediation-playbook-20270904.pdf.

Recommend offering BrightLayer a credit for the window and an option to pin them to Dedicated routing for scheduled integration windows while we harden the mapping rules.

— Rishi
Staff Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: laura.bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@brightlayer.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 4 Sep 2027 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: 429s during our scheduled integration test window

Alex — follow-up with what we applied and next steps. Apologies again for the disruption. Summary: 
- Root cause: routing window mapping regression during a routing service deploy (INF-RTR-3).
- Immediate remediation executed: rollback, counter clear, temporary burst increase (completed 15:48 PDT).
- Next steps we will take (owners and ETA):
  * Rishi — permanent fix to mapping logic and deploy with canary gates (ETA: 2027-09-07).
  * Ben — create a scheduled-test advisory flag that pins BrightLayer to a larger enforcement window for future scheduled runs (ETA: 2027-09-10).
  * Grace — postmortem write-up and credit calculation (ETA: 2027-09-06).

We will credit BrightLayer for the affected token usage during the 15:10–15:25 PDT window; Grace will send the firm credit amount by Monday. Also offering a technical session to walk through client retry tuning and to coordinate any future scheduled stress tests to avoid amplification — optionally we can provide a short-lived Dedicated routing policy for those windows.

Would you be available for a 30-minute call Monday to review the remediation and next steps? Suggested times: Mon 2027-09-06 08:00 or 11:00 PDT.

Thanks for flagging this, and again sorry for the impact.

— Laura
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Johnson <alex@brightlayer.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@brightlayer.com>, maya.singh <maya.singh@consultcloud.io>
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2027 10:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: 429s during our scheduled integration test window

Laura — thanks for the clear summary and for the fast rollback. We can do Monday 11:00 PDT for the call. Appreciate the offer for credits and a temporary Dedicated routing option while we run future validation windows.

Two quick asks before the call:
1) Can Grace confirm the proposed credit amount range? We need an estimate to present internally.
2) Can Rishi share the proposed client-side retry guidance you referred to (initial delay, jitter, max attempts) so our engineers can pre-adjust for scheduled runs?

I'll join the call with our SRE and procurement lead.

— Alex
